projects.name: Redefining the Health System Experience: Enterprise Decision-Making & Value Proposition
projects.objective: Understand enterprise laboratory decision-making, value propositions, ambulatory settings and behavioural segments across health systems.
key_findings: Enterprise laboratory value is judged on access, workflow fit and measurable health-system impact rather than testing price alone.
Physician-network needs can differ materially from central health-system priorities, creating a need for segmented value propositions.
Ambulatory growth increases the importance of service consistency, turnaround visibility and integrated decision support.
projects.executive_implication: Quest should package diagnostics, analytics and service governance into enterprise propositions tailored by decision-maker and care setting.

projects.name: Digital Customer Journey & Solutions Roadmap – Health Systems & Physician Groups
projects.objective: Identify digital touchpoints, workflow friction, interoperability barriers and implementation needs across health systems and physician groups.
key_findings: Workflow integration and onboarding friction are recurring determinants of adoption across both health systems and physician groups.
Digital value depends on reducing handoffs and surfacing status information at the point of work rather than adding another standalone portal.
The quantitative layer indicates that journey pain points vary by customer setting, making segment-specific roadmap prioritization important.
projects.executive_implication: Prioritize interoperability, onboarding simplicity and role-specific workflow support before expanding feature breadth.

artifacts.label: Journey maps, segmentation and analysis workbooks

projects.name: Data Ecosystem Needs
projects.objective: Explore HCP behaviours, AI and next-best-action use cases, population-health analytics, interoperability and digital investment priorities.
key_findings: AI is most credible when embedded into trusted clinical workflows rather than positioned as a standalone capability.
Interoperability and data access remain foundational barriers to realizing analytics and next-best-action value.
Population-health use cases increase demand for longitudinal, governed and context-rich diagnostic data.
projects.executive_implication: Lead with workflow-embedded data products and governance, using interoperability as the foundation for AI-enabled value propositions.

projects.name: Data Ecosystem Needs (Extended Study)
projects.objective: Assess partner and data-ecosystem capabilities, interoperability challenges, priority use cases and partnership opportunities.
key_findings: Partnership value is strongest where external capabilities shorten time-to-value for health-system integration and analytics.
Clear data rights, implementation accountability and workflow ownership are critical to ecosystem adoption.
Partner selection should balance technical fit with the ability to support enterprise governance and scale.
projects.executive_implication: Use a partnership scorecard that weighs interoperability, implementation ownership, data governance and enterprise scalability—not technology fit alone.

projects.name: Lab Stewardship & Analytics Competitive Positioning Research
projects.objective: Identify unmet customer needs, product gaps, competitive positioning, messaging opportunities and make-versus-buy implications for stewardship and analytics.
key_findings: Customers value stewardship when analytics translate into measurable utilization decisions rather than dashboards alone.
Clinical credibility and workflow integration are important differentiators in a market with expanding analytics options.
Evidence-backed decision support creates room for differentiated managed-service and partnership models.
projects.executive_implication: Position stewardship as an outcomes and decision-support proposition supported by analytics, clinical expertise and operational integration.

projects.name: US Consumer Testing Market: Company Profiles Refresh & Expansion 2026
projects.objective: Refresh and expand consumer-testing company profiles across digital health, wearables, telehealth and retail health.
key_findings: Consumer testing competition increasingly blends diagnostics with digital access, subscription models and broader wellness propositions.
Retail and telehealth channels lower access friction but place more weight on simple packaging, trust and follow-through.
Differentiation depends on connecting testing to actionable interpretation rather than selling isolated tests.
projects.executive_implication: Quest should defend trust and clinical credibility while simplifying consumer access and connecting results to longitudinal guidance.

projects.name: Clinical Laboratory Competitive Intelligence — Always On
projects.objective: Maintain an always-on view of competitor moves, product launches, partnerships, financial developments and strategic implications for Quest.
key_findings: Competitive activity is concentrating around precision oncology, health-system integration, AI-enabled workflows and consumer access.
Scale players are using partnerships and acquisitions to increase specialty depth while focused diagnostics companies compete on clinical evidence and data assets.
Quest's strongest differentiation opportunity is to connect broad access and diagnostic scale with workflow-integrated decision support.
projects.executive_implication: Use always-on signals to connect competitor moves to PMR themes and trigger targeted follow-up research when market evidence challenges current assumptions.
